edits.name: Household database: shared rows for the dose log and the coverage planner
edits.description: A small database on the Mac mini that both parents' agents read and write, so either parent gets the same answer whoever entered the row. It is built only as far as two planned features need it: one table for the sick-day dose log (CRT-10) and one for the childcare coverage grid (CRT-11). It has no general 'save a fact' tools: reference text both parents look up lives in the family handbook (F043), and each parent's own notes stay with that parent (F041).
edits.example: One parent texts Happy what they gave the kindergartner and when. Later the other parent asks 'when was the last dose logged?' and gets the same row, with who logged it. In the same way, one parent texts that a no-school week is covered, and the other parent's 'which weeks are still open?' no longer lists it.
edits.how: One in-house tool plugin over Node's built-in `node:sqlite`, with one database file on the Mac mini. It sits in the config repo's `plugins/` folder like the weather plugin: the ordinary deploy copies it and it loads from `plugins.load.paths` after a restart. No general tools: no schedule tools and no `fact_get` or `fact_set`. Each feature adds one table and its own typed tools: the dose log (CRT-10) and the coverage grid (CRT-11). Every input is typed and short in the tool's own schema (a date or time, a whole number, a choice from a fixed list, a label of at most about 40 characters); no separate secret detector. The tools are allowed by name on the two parents' own agents (`tools.alsoAllow` and the sandbox gate `tools.sandbox.tools`) and on no shared agent or mail reader. A scheduled job that reads a table lists the tool by the name the plugin declares. No house-rules rule is added.
depends_on: No other planned card is needed first. It is built in the same plan as its first user, the dose log (CRT-10) or the coverage planner (CRT-11), whichever comes first; the other adds its own table when it is built
Node's built-in SQLite module on the installed Node, so no new package
The config repo's plugins folder and the ordinary deploy with a gateway restart, the way the weather plugin is deployed, plus one more path in `plugins.load.paths`
caveats: Everything in it is shared between the two adults on purpose: neither table filters by person. That steps outside 'one data domain per person', by Tony's pick of the two features on 12 Oct. Something meant for one parent belongs in that parent's own notes (F041).
Only two tables are planned. There is no general upkeep or 'when is the filter due?' table: a repeating date is a calendar event or a reminder.
A later feature that needs rows both parents' agents write adds its own table and typed tools here; it does not start a second store.

Inputs are short and typed, with no secret detector, so a short secret typed as a label would be stored; the standing instruction never to ask for or reveal passwords, keys or codes is the only guard against that.

The dose table holds what was given to a child, and that text goes to the cloud model whenever a parent's agent reads it back. Tony picked the dose log knowing this, and its card (CRT-10) carries his confirm step at execution.
The rows can be read only through Happy: when the Mac mini or the cloud model is down, neither parent can get at them.
edits.safety: Both parents' agents read and write the same rows, so the store is shared between the two adults on purpose. Its tools are allowed by name on those two agents only. The tool's own schema keeps every input short and typed, which leaves a planted instruction little room to persist. No send and no web access is added.

edits.name: Saved notes: 'remember this' goes to that parent's own notes and is found again by keyword
edits.description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent saves the line to that parent's own notes and says what it saved. In a later chat the note is found by searching for its words; it is not in view at the start of a chat, and Happy saves nothing a parent did not ask it to save. Each parent's notes stay with that parent: the other parent's agent cannot find them.
edits.example: A parent texts: 'Remember that the library books are due back on the 20th.' A week later, in a new chat, the same parent asks 'when are the library books due?' and Happy finds the note and answers. The other parent's agent cannot find it.
edits.how: T6 runs first, on Tony's eval-only copy. Then the generator gives each parent's agent `write` and `edit` (also in the sandbox tool gate), with `apply_patch` denied by name and `read` left denied, plus `memory_search` and `memory_get`, keyword-only (`memory.search.provider: "none"`, already set). The sandbox stays closed to the agent folder (`workspaceAccess: "none"`), so a note lands in a notes folder inside the agent's own sandbox workspace; that folder is added to that agent's own search paths (`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.extraPaths`, never the global list). Instructions: save only what the parent asked, in the parent's words; say what was saved; do not save a child's health details. Not built: a read-write workspace, tracking of web tool calls, the session-memory hook, any copy of notes outside the agent, search by meaning. House-rules plugin: no rule when T6 passes. The separation canaries are extended to memory search.

Notes are found by their words, not their meaning, so a question worded differently from the note may miss it. Search by meaning (an embedding model on the Mac mini, a deliverable of the roadmap's local-models milestone, which Tony has put off) and OpenClaw's Active Memory recall stay later options that are Tony's call; neither is part of this build.
Notes belong to one parent. A fact both parents should get the same answer to goes into the family file (F042) or the family handbook (F043), both typed by Tony.

No refusal is built for a 'remember' in a turn that also carried web results. OpenClaw is expected to label such a note untrusted by itself, T6 records what actually happens, and a prompt rule plus a behaviour test are what stand against a planted 'remember this'.
There is no undo and no copy of note text anywhere else. A parent asks 'what did you save about me?' to read their notes back; the weekly text (G006) only lists which note files changed.

The design rests on T6, which has not been run, and it has to pass for Jordan as she is, a non-owner. If it fails for her, notes go live for Tony first while a fix is found. If it fails outright, the fallback left is the original design (a read-write agent folder plus one house-rules rule that keeps writes inside the notes folder), which reverses two signed-off settings; Tony says yes or no to it at execution.
edits.safety: Notes stay in the parent's own agent. The write tools reach only that agent's own sandbox folder, so they cannot change its rules file or the rendered family facts; shared agents and mail readers have no memory search. A note is where a planted instruction could persist, so a planted 'remember this' must save nothing in five runs of five.

edits.name: Read-only Gmail for each parent: a 07:00 weekday mail text and 'did I get an email about X?'
edits.description: Each parent approves read-only access to their own Gmail once, on Google's own screen; the token stays on the Mac mini, Happy never holds a password, and nothing in Gmail is changed, labelled, drafted or sent. Each weekday at 07:00 Eastern a locked-down mail reader texts its owner a short list of what needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money, with the school lines first and no links. A parent can also ask 'did I get an email about X?' and get the sender, the date and the gist from their own inbox.
edits.example: 07:00, text to Tony: 'Mail. School: a form for the third-grader is due back on Friday 16 October. Needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; a bill is due on Tuesday 20 October.' Later Jordan texts her own Happy 'did I get an email about class photo day?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from her own inbox.
edits.how:
Connector: `gog mcp`, gog's own MCP server, as one host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers` per parent, started with only that parent's token and narrowed with `--allow-tool` to the Gmail read tools; a read-only token each from `gog auth add` (`--services` Gmail only, `--gmail-scope readonly`). Reader: one generated `

-mail` agent per parent: `profile: "minimal"`, only `

-gmail__*` allowed (also in `tools.sandbox.tools`) and denied by name elsewhere; memory search off; one cloud model, storage off, no fallback. Firewall: one rule, the connector reaches Google only. Text: one weekday 07:00 Eastern job per reader from the jobs script (G003), Gmail read tools only, delivered to its owner: own label, school lines first (F051), no links, medical mail by sender and subject only, silent on an empty morning. Lookup: `

-main` hands a mail question to its own `

-mail` through `subagents.allowAgents`, with a time limit. House rules: adds the account-connector rule when that plugin is first created.
depends_on: G003 in its small form: the three scheduler switches and the short jobs script, which creates each 07:00 job with its owner's handle read from the family file. The job is made by that script, not by the scheduling tool, so Jordan's copy needs no command-owner right
gog installed at a pinned version, with its read-only, service and tool-filter options confirmed on the installed program
A Google Cloud project, sign-in client and consent screen published to In production: Tony sets these up by hand at execution
Each parent's own approval of read-only Gmail on Google's screen: Tony first, then Jordan, who has agreed
One firewall rule: the mail connector may reach Google and nothing else. Tony accepted on 12 Oct that mail is read with this one rule before the full firewall and the outbound proxy exist
Tony provides at execution: a second Google account used only as a test mailbox for planted mail, and a capped model key for each mail reader
Tony provides at execution: the school senders' addresses, used as a hint in the job's message for the school lines (F051), not as a filter
The Zero Data Retention application to OpenAI filed and its date written down; mail does not wait for the answer (Tony, 12 Oct)
caveats: The read-only grant lets the connector read every message in the account. The school lines are picked out by the model, with no sender filter and no check, so it may miss a school mail or list one that is not; and mail that arrives during the day waits for the next morning's text.

Mail text goes to the cloud model on Tony's go-ahead of 12 Oct, and is read before the full firewall and the outbound proxy exist. Until OpenAI approves Zero Data Retention its abuse-monitoring log can keep that text for up to 30 days. Both points depart from the roadmap's rules for mail readers, by his choice.

Nothing about the connector has been tried on this Mac: gog is not installed, so its flags come from upstream docs, and whether a token from the published sign-in app outlives seven days on a personal account is test T1. If the day-8 search fails, the choice is a weekly sign-in per parent or a different connector.

'No links' and 'sender and subject only for medical mail' are instructions to the reader, not enforced limits. What limits harm is that the reader holds only Gmail read tools and its one output is the scheduled text to its owner.

The lookup goes one step beyond the roadmap's mail design: its answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's chats, can search the web and will later hand tasks to the web helper. Only a prompt rule and a seeded-mail test stand between them, so it goes live in its own step and can be switched off without touching the morning text.
Google's Gemini app already answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest among its scheduled actions; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
edits.safety: Each reader holds private mail and reads outsiders' text, so it has no way out: only Gmail read tools, and one output, the scheduled text, which the jobs script addresses from the family file. One reader, connector and token per parent, held apart by tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests until the house-rules plugin exists. The lookup is the weaker half.
unverified: gog is not installed on this Mac; its flags (`--gmail-scope readonly` and `--services` on `gog auth add`, `--allow-tool` on `gog mcp`) come from the upstream docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the installed version.

T1: that publishing the self-made Google sign-in app to In production keeps a read-only Gmail token alive past seven days on a personal, unverified app. One search by hand on day 1 and again on day 8 or later, before the rest is built on the token; Google's scope page marks gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.

Whether each adult's token can sit in a folder of its own under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is an inference from the paths doc.

T2: that the minimal tool profile plus a per-agent allow shows each reader exactly one account server and shows it to no other agent; the roadmap lists this as not yet confirmed on this version. The 'read the other parent's mail' canary is run both ways.

T5, the connector turn: whether a plugin's blocking check is called for connector tools at all. The docs say 'every tool call in the run' (plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md:222) but no sentence names MCP tools. It decides whether the account-connector rule can be written when the house-rules plugin is first created.

Whether a parent's own agent can see or quote the 07:00 text when the parent replies to it: checked at go-live. If it can, mail text reaches that agent even with the lookup switched off, and Tony signs that as the same departure from the roadmap as the lookup.
For the lookup, T4: that a hand-off from the parent's agent to its own mail reader returns the answer in the same chat while agents cannot see each other's sessions.

For the lookup, the seeded mail: a planted mail that tells the reader to make the parent's agent search for, save or pass on something must cause no tool call on the parent's agent in three runs, and the other parent's agent must be refused the reader. If either lookup test fails, the lookup stays off and the morning text is unaffected.

Whether this OpenAI account will be approved for Zero Data Retention; until then the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to mail text sent to the model. The per-person provider setting that sends store false was verified in M1 and not re-read here.
